what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Russia in Poland: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 3006 Russian asylum seekers in Poland, 3.4% of all asylum seekers from Russia.
Refugees from Russia, a separate group, live mostly in France, Germany, the United States and Austria.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over Chechnya territory in Russia from 1999 to 2007 and over Caucasus Emirate territory from 2007 to 2015.
It also records an interstate armed conflict between Russia and Ukraine from 2022 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2002 at 1880 asylum seekers, and the figure was at its highest, 5653, at the end of 2007.
It fell to a low in 2021 and then rose; the main years of displacement in the data include 2007 to 2008 and 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Poland.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for Poland only.
